concepts.title: Parallel Lines: Same Direction, Never Meeting
concepts.definition: Parallel lines run in the same direction and keep the same distance everywhere, so however far they are drawn they never meet, like the opposite edges of a ruler or railway tracks.
concepts.key_idea: Parallelism is about direction: same direction plus constant gap means no meeting, ever.

concepts.title: Intersecting Lines and the Angles They Make
concepts.definition: When two lines cross, four angles form at the crossing: angles on one side of a line fill a straight angle of 180 degrees, and the angles opposite each other at the crossing are equal.
concepts.key_idea: A crossing obeys two quiet laws: each straight side totals 180 degrees, and opposite angles are twins.

solution_steps.explain: Angles filling one side of a straight line total 180 degrees.

concepts.title: Perpendicular Lines: The Right-Angle Crossing
concepts.definition: When two intersecting lines make a right angle of 90 degrees at their crossing, they are perpendicular; the four angles are then equal right angles, as at the corners of a page.
concepts.key_idea: Perpendicular is the fairest crossing: all four angles share the same 90 degrees.

concepts.title: Lines Across a Line: Transversals
concepts.definition: A line drawn across two or more lines is a transversal; it makes eight angles, and matching positions at the two crossings reveal equal or related pairs, a first look at the geometry of parallel lines.
concepts.key_idea: A transversal is a scanner: it copies the angle pattern from one crossing to the other when the lines are parallel.
